title: AC-STEM, Photoluminescence, and Raman Characterization of Novel MoxWx-1S2 Alloys
content: Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are of interest across several sub-fields of physics owing to their exciting electrical and optical properties, including a band gap that evolves from indirect in the bulk and few layers to direct in a single layer [1, 2]. MoS2 and WS2 are two TMDs that have been extensively studied within the 2D TMD community, and both are particularly promising materials due to large current on/off ratios in field-effect transistors (FETs) [3, 4], strong photoluminescence [5, 6], and methods of large-area synthesis of monolayers [7, 8]. Though these 2D TMDs are themselves promising materials, space remains to further engineer the optoelectronic properties of 2D TMDs through controlled doping with different metals.
